summary: Correction pass over the RESEARCH-OS-MIGRATION-design claim, superseding 2026-07-11T083329Z_research-os-migration_RESEARCH-OS-MIGRATION-design (which WAS previously approved via approval receipt 2026-07-11T083643Z_user-approval_RESEARCH-OS-MIGRATION-design and committed at 3021f1279ce8cdd9d5dd728e683d8376fb0f83ea), in response to a user-identified source-snapshot contradiction: the accepted contract's history range hard-coded its upper endpoint to ed50db0d62b755cd7aae9f00228665ba0cdb5750, but this very design contract (and its own claim/approval receipts) was subsequently committed at 3021f1279ce8cdd9d5dd728e683d8376fb0f83ea -- AFTER that endpoint -- so following the old range literally would have omitted the contract itself, its superseded design claim, its active design claim, and its approval receipt from the migration inventory, directly violating the 'entire automation directory / all historical receipts' policy. After capture, the source repository is explicitly FROZEN for the remainder of the migration implementation -- any change to source HEAD, tracked state, branch, or remote-tracking relationship before target-side validation completes aborts the migration. f64d5626d3b159f85988668f0a86281035678e93 (the repository's own root commit) remains the fixed, permanent lower bound (repositories.source.research_os_history_floor) since, unlike a moving upper endpoint, a repository's root commit can never become stale. A new explicit rule states: re-running the migration with a different SOURCE_SNAPSHOT_SHA than a prior attempt must fail visibly unless a NEW migration claim explicitly supersedes the earlier attempt's claim and documents the new snapshot and why it differs -- never a silent, undocumented re-snapshot.
